sections.label: Validation order (before ANY execution)
items: 1. Does the named tool exist in the registry?
2. Are all required arguments present (and correctly typed)?
3. Has this call ID already succeeded (idempotency check)?
Only after all three does the handler actually run.

sections.label: Idempotent executor pattern
Cache successes, never failures
items: A success gets cached against the call ID: a repeat returns the cached result, the handler never re-runs.
A failure must NOT be cached: the side effect never happened, so a genuine retry deserves a real second attempt.

sections.label: Two validation layers
items: **Business-rule validation**: does the VALUE make sense for this specific case? (e.g. a refund amount within the order's actual total)
A call can pass schema validation and still be unsafe to execute.

sections.label: Common mistakes
items: Checking the idempotency cache AFTER calling the handler instead of before.
Caching a result before knowing if the handler actually succeeded.
Treating schema-valid as "safe to execute" without a business-rule check.

sections.label: Implementation checklist
checklist: Unknown tool names are rejected before any handler runs.
A cached success returns without re-invoking the handler.
A raised error is never written to the idempotency cache.
